Lucifer the light bringer was originally created by God himself in Christian mythology as far as I know. He was supposed to be the most beautiful and intelligent of all the angels created by God, but he yearned for more than what was his place, he disagreed with God and wanted power for himself. As such, he lead an uprising against God, but was defeated and vanquished to Hell where he was to remain eternally. This is covered in books like 'Paradise Lost' by John Milton, or 'Dante's Inferno' by Dante Aligheri, and of course in the bible itself. In Paradise Lost is where the phrase 'It is better to reign in Hell than serve in heaven' originates, and helps to give a bit of insight into his character. He desired power.

Personally, I think it runs parallel with other mythologies, namely the Titans in Greek mythology. Lucifer is hinted as being the snake in the Garden of Eden story in the bible (if you read the bible in its entirety, Satan really doesn't come up very often at all. It's mostly other literature like Paradise Lost that we see much of him), which is where I derive the similarity. In the Greek mythology, the titan Prometheus gives fire to humans and is cast down and punished for what should be eternity by Zeus. Despite the redemption story there that doesn't occur in Christian mythology (Hercules eventually rescues Prometheus from his fate of having his liver devoured by an eagle every single day by killing the eagle and breaking the chain keeping Prometheus attached to the rock), the desire of both Prometheus and the snake (Satan) to bestow knowledge to humans which incurs the wrath of God stays the same. The snake (Satan) is the one that gets Eve to eat the apple from the tree of knowledge, and Prometheus brings fire, mathematics, navigation, architecture, etc. to humans.
